description: The Prada Canapa is the house's canvas tote, named for the Italian word for hemp. It is a lightweight, vintage-leaning shopper in sturdy woven canvas with leather trim and the Prada triangle logo, built more for daily errands than evening. Because it is fabric rather than leather, it has long sat at a lower price point than Prada's leather bags.

The Louis Vuitton Geronimos is a compact body bag worn at the waist or across the chest, most often seen in Damier Ebène coated canvas. It has a curved, slim profile with a front zip pocket and an adjustable belt-style strap. It has since been discontinued, so it turns up mainly on the resale market.

The Balenciaga Town is a small bag in the house's Motorcycle family, the slouchy studded line Nicolas Ghesquière introduced in the early 2000s. It sits between the smaller First and the popular City in size, with the same soft lambskin, tassels and mirror. Think of it as a City scaled down for a lighter everyday carry.

The Louis Vuitton Sully is a soft Monogram hobo with a rounded, gathered shape and a single shoulder strap. It comes in PM and MM sizes, with the classic natural cowhide trim and gold-tone hardware. It reads as an easy, unstructured everyday shoulder bag rather than a formal top-handle.

The Dior Diorever is a structured top-handle bag introduced under Maria Grazia Chiuri, built around a flip-lock closure stamped with the CD initials. It has a clean trapezoidal body, a top handle and a detachable strap for shoulder or crossbody wear. Dior showed it across leathers and exotics before phasing it out, so it now lives mainly on resale.

The Saint Laurent Belle de Jour is a flat envelope clutch from the Yves Saint Laurent era, most recognizable in glossy patent leather with a large embossed YSL logo on the front. It is a simple, structured evening piece with a fold-over flap and no strap. It dates to Stefano Pilati's tenure at the house, roughly 2004 to 2012, though a precise launch year is not firmly documented.

The Hermès Constance To Go is a long wallet built to double as a slim clutch or wallet-on-strap. It carries the house's H-shaped clasp on the flap, with card slots, a zip change purse and interior pockets inside, and a removable strap for crossbody wear. Hermès has offered it in leathers like Epsom and Evercolor across its permanent color range.

The Chloé Nile is the equestrian-inspired bag Clare Waight Keller designed toward the end of her time at the house, defined by a curved metal ring handle over a saddle-shaped body. It typically has a top handle plus a long strap, in smooth and suede leathers with light gold hardware. A bracelet-handle version followed for Summer 2017 and became a heavy street-style favorite.

The Marc Jacobs Snapshot is a small crossbody styled after a vintage camera bag, with a boxy double-compartment body and the oversized MJ double-J logo on the front. It is known for graphic color-blocking and a webbed strap, and sits at an accessible price for a designer bag. It debuted on the Marc Jacobs runway and became one of the brand's signature sellers.

The Louis Vuitton Sirius is a boxy soft-sided travel bag, part of the house's classic luggage line and offered in sizes such as 45, 55 and 70. It has a structured rectangular shape, dual top handles, a wraparound zip and the padlock and leather trim of the Keepall family. Unlike the Keepall Bandoulière, the traditional Sirius is carried by its handles rather than a shoulder strap.

The LV Biker is a slouchy carryall Nicolas Ghesquière designed for Louis Vuitton's Spring/Summer 2025 collection, launched in February 2025. It has a soft, gathered body with biker-jacket hardware cues and comes in MM, PM and Nano sizes. It arrived with heavy visibility on ambassadors like Lisa and was quickly tipped as a potential new house hit.

The Louis Vuitton Porte-Documents Voyage is a structured briefcase built for work travel, offered in Taiga leather and Monogram canvases. It has dual top handles, a zip closure, a padded interior roomy enough for a 13-inch laptop, and a detachable adjustable shoulder strap. It is one of LV's long-running men's business bags.

The Louis Vuitton Popincourt is a compact Monogram shoulder bag with a rounded, structured body and short handles, often seen in an east-west (wide and low) shape. It carries the classic Monogram canvas with natural leather trim and gold-tone hardware. It is a vintage-era style now found mainly secondhand.

The Louis Vuitton Buci is a modern crossbody flap in the house's textured Epi leather, with smooth leather corners and edges and a chain-and-leather strap. It has a clean, compact rectangular shape and reads as an everyday shoulder or crossbody bag. It sits toward the more accessible end of LV's leather bags.

The Versace Virtus is a line built around the house's Barocco V hardware, a glossy gold-tone V framed by acanthus scrollwork. It appears across shapes including flap shoulder bags, hobos and evening bags, often on V-quilted leather. Versace frames the V as a symbol of virtue and courage.

The Saint Laurent Uptown is a sharp, structured design in grain de poudre embossed leather, carrying the metal Cassandre YSL logo on the flap. It exists as both a top-handle tote and a flat envelope pouch, with clean lines and gold-tone hardware, and is an Anthony Vaccarello-era style. The pouch version often includes a removable strap so it works as a shoulder bag or clutch.

The Louis Vuitton Chelsea is a large vintage-era shoulder bag, most often seen in Damier Ebène coated canvas with leather double handles and a top zip. It has a roomy, structured tote shape made for carrying more than the everyday essentials. It is discontinued and now a secondhand find.

The Louis Vuitton Bosphore is a Monogram line for hands-free carry, spanning a slim messenger/crossbody and a belt (bum) bag. The pieces use classic Monogram canvas with leather trim, a zip or buckle closure and an adjustable strap. It is a discontinued style now mostly seen on resale.

The Moynat Réjane is one of the house's signature top-handle bags, named for the French stage actress Réjane, for whom Pauline Moynat created an early version in 1903. It has a rounded, structured silhouette with dual top handles and clean, understated hardware, a nod to Moynat's trunk-making heritage. The modern Réjane revives that historic model.

The Louis Vuitton Marelle is best known in its Pochette Marelle form, a Monogram canvas waist bag with a buckled belt and a front zip pocket. It has a slim, curved body meant to sit at the waist or wear across the body. The vintage Pochette Marelle is a discontinued piece found on resale; LV has since reused the Marelle name on newer designs.

The Louis Vuitton Monceau is a structured vintage top-handle bag, typically a boxy shape in Monogram canvas or Epi leather with short handles and a front flap or zip pockets. It reads as a polished, briefcase-adjacent day bag. It is a discontinued style that turns up mainly secondhand and is often called an underrated vintage pick.

The Louis Vuitton Verona is a structured shoulder tote in Damier Ebène coated canvas, with rolled leather handles, a top zip and a red fabric-lined interior. It comes in PM and MM sizes and sits comfortably on the shoulder for everyday use. It is a discontinued style found mainly on resale.

The Louis Vuitton Rivoli is a structured top-handle bag, seen both as a vintage briefcase-style piece and as a later handbag in Damier Ebène with a rounded body, top handles and a removable strap. The hardware includes the classic LV padlock. Versions carry gold-tone hardware and the house's leather trim.

The Louis Vuitton Greenwich is a structured top-handle satchel, seen in both vintage Epi leather and Damier Ebène versions, with a boxy body, dual handles and gold-tone hardware. Some versions come with a padlock, key and detachable strap for crossbody wear. It is a classic day-bag shape now largely found secondhand.

The Louis Vuitton Victoire is a flap shoulder bag in Monogram canvas trimmed with colored calfskin, closed by a gold-tone press-lock. Its long sliding chain-and-leather strap lets it be worn on the shoulder or crossbody, and the interior is divided into gusseted compartments. It is a more recent, dressier design than LV's vintage lines.

The Louis Vuitton Reade is a small, glossy tote in Monogram Vernis patent leather, with short handles and a rounded body, dating to the Marc Jacobs Y2K era of the house. It comes in petite sizes like the PM and in the bright, candy-like Vernis colors of that period. It is discontinued and now a nostalgic resale piece.

The Loro Piana Extra Pocket is a soft, minimalist pouch in the house's supple calfskin and other fine leathers, with clean lines, a zip top and a slim removable belt. That belt lets it be worn at the waist or crossbody, or carried as a pouch. It is understated by design, with the quality in the leather rather than in logos.

The Louis Vuitton Camera Box is a structured crossbody that borrows the Petite Malle's trunk details, including the S-lock closure, metallic corners and rivets. It has a compact boxy body, usually in Monogram canvas with a mix of finishes, and a detachable adjustable strap. It reads as a modern, collectible take on LV's trunk heritage.

The Louis Vuitton Petit Palais is a structured tote in Monogram canvas trimmed with natural leather and lined in red textile. It has a clean, ladylike shape with top handles and a detachable strap for shoulder or crossbody wear. It is one of LV's more polished everyday totes.
